source: docs/ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.md §8 (preview column); IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN Task 13 'Cut 1 release gate' and Task 18
verdict_reason: Both live gates failed. The first (2026-10-26): the installed host updated itself mid-run, the machine slept, and update_task replies hit their output allowance under a reasoning curator. The second (2026-10-29, engine 0.1.0.dev1, Claude Code 2.1.310 live-certified): no curator call hit the output cap, but the lid was closed overnight and Wi-Fi dropped on waking, R4's working agents wrote CLAUDE.md in both arms, R4's stale fact was delivered without a freshness label, and fresh-session reuse and the changed-condition revision were not shown; live §5.1 support and recall await reviewer labels. A scripted/recorded run is never a pass

items.detail: Every deterministic suite passes locally on Python 3.12/3.13/3.14 and in CI on Linux, macOS and Windows (see the Task 18 checkpoint); the manifest maps every one of the 67 preview IDs and their §2.1 partial variants to existing tests. No case is marked passed: several preview variants include live-host parts (A27, A28, A29, A30, A61, A67 and the live delivery paths) that need a passing live run. B1 cleared on native Windows, and both live gates failed (2026-10-26, 2026-10-29).
items.blocker: live variants (no live gate has passed)

items.detail: Live-certified on native Windows on 2026-10-23 (the owner's run): the anthropic_messages curator route (provider probe and runtime check exit 0) and all four delivery paths of Claude Code 2.1.309 through the real engine and the installed hooks (3/3 positives and 3/3 clean negatives each). On 2026-10-28 the same held for engine 0.1.0.dev1 on a fresh pilot: the route (provider probe and runtime check certified) and all four delivery paths of Claude Code 2.1.310 (3/3 and 3/3 each). Linux and macOS are not observed live.
items.blocker: Linux and macOS live not observed

items.detail: Two live 12-scenario comparative smoke runs, with the workload days and demonstrations, have failed. The first (2026-10-23 to 2026-10-26): five candidates refused after the host updated itself mid-run, the laptop slept, and most waits stalled on update_task's output allowance. The second (2026-10-28 to 2026-10-29, engine 0.1.0.dev1): none of 144 curator calls hit the output cap; the lid was closed overnight and Wi-Fi dropped on waking, which stopped L3, L4, R1, R2 and R3's candidates; R4's agents wrote CLAUDE.md in both arms (contaminated); R4's stale fact was delivered without a freshness label (conflict/uncertainty preservation 0/1); R2's candidate was scored failed by an oracle false negative (fixed, decision 0028 item 17); fresh-session reuse and the changed-condition revision were not shown; two of three workload days exhausted the ordinary input pool at about 4 h. The scripted/recorded run (mechanics only) remains in docs/evaluations/preview-recorded-2026-10-21/. Preview may only be published as an explicitly experimental build until a live gate passes.
items.blocker: a live gate that passes, after the owner's decisions in the 2026-10-29 checkpoint (R4's agent-written instruction files and freshness label, fresh-session reuse with a capable agent, the input pool), on a machine that stays awake and online, with reviewer labels for live support and recall

items.detail: Deterministic and kill/restart suites pass for backup, verified restore, forgetting with suppression-aware restore, pin-aware retention (with derived revision-body aging), the operator-command guard and cross-installation isolation; the scripted §6.1 demonstrations reproduce forgetting/restore and isolation end to end. Migration/upgrade and transfers are full-only.

tools/build_release.py checks the runtime closure of requirements.lock with each package's declared license against docs/release/DEPENDENCIES.json, the wheel's contents against src/recalith, and the absence of foreign copyright headers (no upstream source is adapted, so no THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md ships). The project's own license is not declared in pyproject.toml: that is an owner decision and a publication blocker, recorded under release_artifacts.

docs/OPERATIONS.md separates automatic operation, fallback operation (each degraded condition with what still works and its status reason) and missing capabilities (the 16 deferred features and the other full-only forms).

The report format carries unsuccessful runs, all seven §5.2 measures, the observed native-memory setting, scenario authorship, pilot status and the §6.2 arithmetic labeled as illustrative, actual costs, limitations and no superiority claim; the recorded run's report is checked into docs/evaluations/. Both live reports (failed gates) are checked in sanitized under docs/evaluations/preview-live-2026-10-26/ and docs/evaluations/preview-live-2026-10-29/.
All five Review focus items rechecked at the Task 18 gate, with the cross-component tests rerun (see the Task 18 checkpoint in docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md).
focus_items: same source event twice across a crash: one support root, one effect
quoted or repeated through agent memory: no added authority or corroboration
correction or forget before the final delivery fence: old guidance excluded, in-flight emission bounded
paths across Windows, worktrees and relocation: only registered boundaries
provider or host version change: capability rechecked, no silent autonomy claim

items.detail: Reported explicitly: the fast-path import audits (tests/platform/test_hook_imports.py), private-path restriction coverage (probed_limited on the installed host; preview installs none), the three default-budget workload days (recorded mode, with the input-estimate pool exhaustion they show) and fresh post-forget recovery (the post-forget verified backup and the forget/restore kill/restart matrix).
recalith status / health(ctx) report release_profile claude_preview, every required and optional capability with its reason, and these 16 deferred features unavailable with deferred_full_release.

tools/measure_release_latency.py and tools/measure_worker_latency.py run the §7 populations per native platform: this container and .github/workflows/measure.yml on Linux, macOS and Windows runners. Every healthy target is met on every platform on the final code (b3f1f1f) in two full measure runs (21 and 24). Hook spawn-to-exit p95: Linux 53.0/59.3 ms warm and 46.6/59.8 ms cold; macOS 92.0/126.1 warm and 62.9/81.7 cold; Windows 138.7/135.0 warm and 137.8/148.1 cold. Warm delivered ≥ 0.998 and cold 1.0 everywhere. This container: 108.5 ms warm and 105.9 ms cold, 500/500 delivered. Typed event to working state, p95 with 5 s idle polling: Linux 4.48/4.47 s; macOS 4.55/4.39 s; Windows 4.82/4.92 s (n=20 each); Windows 4.75 and 4.62 s in two 60-trial runs (22 and 23); this container 4.74 s (n=100). Idle worker over 600 s: under 0.24 % of one core and ≤ 47 MiB everywhere. Decision 0022 attributed the earlier Windows typed-state misses. The measurement planned arrivals from a stale idle status and read poll durations one poll late, which made a cadence drift appear that the worker does not have. The remaining Windows outliers are single ingesting polls stalled by the runner's storage (1–5 s), and the WAL checkpoint was moved off the typed-state path. Targets, n, denominators and the arrival model are unchanged (the arrival planning is now stricter). Live trials stay with B1.

Every kill/restart family at RECALITH_CRASH_REPS=20 (100 is for a release candidate, which this is not): 13 families, 128 failpoint cases × 20 reps, 128 passed in 6343.01 s on Linux (Task 18 checkpoint). The retention family gained retention.after_record_aging, and a deliberate mutation there was caught only by this matrix. macOS and Windows run the same families at the default 3 repetitions in CI; the 20-repetition run is Linux only. Decision 0022 added worker.before_checkpoint and worker.after_checkpoint. Every worker family plus capture (125 cases) passed again at 20 repetitions on the final tree (71 passed in 3044.07 s and 54 passed in 2886.46 s).
tools/build_release.py and .github/workflows/release.yml build the wheel and sdist with SHA-256 digests and a release manifest. They are unsigned, and nothing is tagged or published.
